statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-86415: libcurl's connection reuse did not take the automatic client certificate option (CURLSSLOPT_AUTO_CLIENT_CERT) into account, so a cached Schannel connection already authenticated with an automatically chosen client certificate could be handed to a transfer redirected to a different origin (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-86415.html). curl's advisory says the flaw only affects curl built with Schannel, a TLS backend available only on Windows; it affects 8.21.0 to 8.22.0 and was fixed in 8.23.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/00271cfcb95b6481a1f91ce0a0dad5d64d2e89a9. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 published in the DHI Alpine main repository as of 2026-11-28 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, libcurl.so.4 links OpenSSL (libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3) and no other TLS library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from schannel.c and schannel_verify.c define no symbols, while the same check finds 50 to 56 symbols defined in the object built from openssl.c. The Schannel backend is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present. Packages published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which needs credentials, were not inspected.

The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.24 published in the DHI Alpine main repository as of 2026-11-28 are builds of curl 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.22.0-r1 and 8.23.0-r0, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the libcurl and curl-static packages of every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, libcurl.so.4 links OpenSSL (libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3) and no other TLS library, and in the static libcurl.a the objects built from schannel.c and schannel_verify.c define no symbols, while the same check finds 52 to 56 symbols defined in the object built from openssl.c. The Schannel backend is not built, so the vulnerable code is not present. Packages published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which needs credentials, were not inspected.
